# Dhammapada (Dhp)

**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Dhammapada

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammapada* is an ancient verse text of the Khuddaka-nikāya consisting of 423 verses arranged into thematic chapters [Hirakawa 1990]. Regarded as one of the oldest texts in the Khuddaka-nikāya, it expresses universal and early Indian ethical wisdom; many of its stanzas are shared with non-Buddhist Indian works, including the *Mahābhārata*, *Manusmṛti*, *Hitopadeśa*, *Garuḍapurāṇa*, and *Yogabhāṣya* [Hirakawa 1990; Lamotte 1988]. The text has become one of the most widely read and translated Buddhist scriptures [Huber 2008; Sueki 2012]. In the Theravāda tradition it is preserved alongside the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, whose traditional attribution to Buddhaghosa has been questioned due to stylistic distinctiveness [Burlingame 1921; Gaffney 2003]. Verses of the *Dhammapada* are also frequently cited in other Pali works, such as the *Jātakanidāna* [Gaffney 2003].
